column3: NKJV renders “the one tooth was a pillar” as “the front of one,” and has “Gibeah” where the Hebrew has “Geba.”
Close to the Hebrew; “a trembling of God” is rendered “a very great trembling.”
Close to the Hebrew; NKJV follows the Hebrew “ark of God” rather than the Septuagint’s “ephod.”
Close to the Hebrew; “his eyes brightened” is rendered “his countenance brightened.”
Close to the Hebrew; “my eyes brightened” is rendered “my countenance has brightened.”
